name: solid Ar at 80 K
paper: A. C. Sinnock and B. L. Smith, "Refractive indices of the condensed inert gases", Phys. Rev. 181 (1969) 1297–1307, DOI 10.1103/PhysRev.181.1297
licence: CC0 1.0 (the refractiveindex.info database, M. N. Polyanskiy, Sci. Data 11, 94 (2024)); reduced values
reduction: n linear and k linear in log k in wavelength between the source's rows, onto 380–780 nm every 5 nm, to six significant figures, with k = 0 stated (the source gives n only). The source's rows are 361.2–643.9 nm, so its 643.9 nm value, n 1.2693, is held over 643.9–780 nm; a Cauchy line fitted by least squares to the source's nine rows (residuals under 7 × 10⁻⁵) gives 1.2682 at 780 nm, so the hold runs at most 0.0011 high. 80 K, as ruled (decision-r08-t5d ruling 3), lies near Ar's triple point (83.8 K), where Ar saturates in a bar-class atmosphere; the source's table at 83.81 K lies 0.0020 lower at 546.1 nm and its 40 K table about 0.016 higher, and Ar's temperature dependence is not modelled. Grace et al. 2017's Sellmeier fit, which also ends short (660 nm), is not taken
